data.copy:
My Zepbound results shocked everyone. But the REAL shock came at 9:13 PM on a Tuesday.

My 14-year-old daughter walked into my closet and found me sitting on the carpet in my underwear.

Surrounded by seven pairs of jeans.

Not one of them fit.

She didn't say anything.

She just slid down the doorframe.

Sat down next to me.

And put her hand on my knee.

"Mom..."

Her voice cracked.

"Please tell me you're not going back on the shots."

I burst into tears.

Because she'd watched this movie twice already.

She'd seen me crash at her 10th birthday party.

She'd held my hand at her 12th when I couldn't fit into anything but her dad's old t-shirts.

She'd watched me disappear from the camera at her dance recitals.

And here I was.

On the closet floor again.

I wiped my face and held up one of the jeans.

"Baby. These jeans aren't too small."

"They're too big."

She looked at me like I was speaking Mandarin.

"But... you're not on the shots?"

"I haven't touched them in almost a year."

That's when I realized I'd never told my own daughter what I was doing differently.

========

Let me back up a sec.

Because if you're on the shots right now, or thinking about it, or just stopped and feel the hunger creeping back... you need to hear this.

The shots are a miracle.

I will fight anyone who says otherwise.

It's literally the first thing in 30 years of dieting that actually WORKED.

Not "worked if you also ate 1200 calories and ran 5 miles daily."

Actually worked.

Like magic.

Like the answer to every prayer I'd whispered into my pillow at 2 AM after another binge.

I could have one bite of cake at a party. ONE BITE.

My coworkers thought I'd had gastric bypass. Nope.

Just a weekly injection that finally made my brain work like a thin person's brain.

data.copy:
My Ozempic results shocked everyone. But the REAL shock was 6 months after stopping

Last Tuesday at 11:47 PM, I found my husband sitting on our bathroom floor, holding my box of Ozempic pens, tears streaming down his face.

"I can't watch you go through this again," he whispered.

He wasn't talking about the injections.

He was talking about what happened the last two times I stopped.

========

See, I've been on Ozempic three times now.

>>First time: Lost 38 pounds. 

Stopped because insurance cut me off. 

Gained back 52 pounds in 11 weeks. 

Yes, you read that right. 

Gained back MORE than I lost.

>>Second time: Lost 41 pounds. 

Stopped because of the side effects. 

The sulfur burps were so bad my daughter's friends wouldn't come over. 

The constipation... let's just say I have the ER bills to prove it. 

Gained everything back plus 8 pounds.

>>Third time: Currently down 47 pounds. 

Been off Ozempic for 9 months. 

Haven't gained back a single pound.

My husband was crying because he thought I was about to start round four.

I sat down next to him on the cold tile floor.

"Babe, I haven't touched these in almost a year."

He looked at me like I was speaking Mandarin. 

"But... you're still thin?"

That's when I realized I'd never actually told him what I'd been doing differently.

========

Let me back up a sec.  

Because if you're on Ozempic right now, or thinking about it, or just stopped and feel the hunger creeping back... you need to hear this.

Ozempic is a miracle. 

I will fight anyone who says otherwise.

It's literally the first thing in 30 years of dieting that actually WORKED. 

Not "worked if you also ate 1200 calories and ran 5 miles daily." 

Actually worked. 

Like magic. 

Like the answer to every prayer I'd whispered into my pillow at 2 AM after another binge.

The food noise - that constant mental chatter of "eat eat eat eat" - went SILENT.

For the first time since puberty, I could walk past a bakery without my brain short-circuiting…

data.caption: Still Restless On Gabapentin?
data.copy:
I've taken gabapentin for my restless legs for two years.

I started at 300 milligrams.

I'm at 900 now, and my neurologist already wants to go higher.

That's how it works with these meds.

It helps, so you stay on it.

Then it stops holding, so they bump the dose.

Then that stops holding, so they bump it again.

I read about a man on twelve pills a night, three thousand six hundred milligrams, still feeling the electricity in his legs.

That's the road I'm on, and everyone on it says the same thing.

It never goes down.

Only up.

I'd already watched where that road ends.

My father walked it for eleven years, six dose increases, and the electricity was still in his legs the week he died, his mind somewhere I still don't have the words for.

And nobody warns you what the climb does to your head.

I can't focus.

People tell me things and I need it repeated three or four times before it sticks.

I lose words in the middle of a sentence.

The fizzing still starts by midnight.

I'm just too foggy now to fight it.

I spent forty years as an engineer, solving problems where imprecision had a cost.

So when my own mind started slipping and I couldn't say why, I stopped asking how high the dose could go and started asking why it had to keep climbing at all.

The gabapentin was never aimed at the fizzing in my legs.

It was aimed at my brain's ability to feel it.

And that is not where the problem lives.

My name is Robert. I'm 63.

Those forty years were spent designing load-bearing systems. Hospitals, schools, three bridges in this state that will outlast me.

Work that punished imprecision.

If your math was wrong, people died.

You learned to check.

You learned to verify.

You trusted nothing you hadn't stress-tested from every angle.

My brain was the tool I spent my entire adult life sharpening.

My colleagues used to say I could run a structural analysis in my head faster than the junior engineers could set up their software.

My wife says I never forgot anything…

data.copy:
I found the Ziploc bag while I was digging for the tire pressure gauge. Ovulation tests, dozens of them, rubber-banded into months, every strip dated in my wife's handwriting. March. April. May. She hasn't said the word "trying" out loud since Christmas. But she never stopped.

I sat in her car in our garage holding that bag for a long time.

Then I put it back exactly the way I found it, went inside, and told her dinner was ready. Because that's what we do in our house now. We protect each other from the things we're both carrying.

Let me back up.

My name is Tom. I'm 42. I fix heating and cooling systems for a living, which means I spend my days in basements and attics finding the one part that's quietly failing inside a system everybody assumed was fine.

My wife is Jess. She's 38. We met at a bowling alley on Secor Road in 2011 because her league needed a sub, and I threw three straight gutter balls trying to impress her, and she wrote her number on my scoresheet next to the word "yikes."

We started trying for a baby a little over three years ago.

I need you to understand something about my wife before I tell you the rest. Jess is the smartest person in our house and it is not close. When she decides to learn something, she learns all of it. When we bought this place she read foundation-repair forums for a month and then argued the inspector into a corner, politely. So when I tell you she ran this the way she runs everything, I mean protocols, spreadsheets, appointments, apps. I mean she can still quote you her numbers from two years ago from memory.

Year one, she shared everything with me. Too much, honestly. I knew words no HVAC guy needs to know.

Year two, the sharing thinned out. The updates got shorter. "Fine." "Same." "Don't worry about it."

And then at Christmas her little sister stood up at the dinner table holding her wine glass and announced she was pregnant. First try. Total accident. Isn't life funny.

data.copy:
Ik ben 32 en al 2 jaar vrijgezel. Niet omdat ik niemand kan vinden, maar omdat ik bacteriële vaginose krijg na elke keer seks.

En dat was niet eens het ergste.

Het ergste was wat BV met mijn leven deed.

Het verwoestte mijn vorige relatie. 

2 jaar samen. Kapot in 8 maanden.

Ik heb 4 verschillende gynaecologen gezien. Elke arts schreef me antibiotica voor. 

En elke keer kwam het gewoon weer terug.

Laat me je vertellen hoe het begon...

Het begon 5 jaar geleden. Ik had een vriend. 

We waren 2 jaar samen.

De seks was goed. Alles was normaal.

Tot ik plots, na een keer seks, een vreemde geur merkte.

Iets wat ik nooit eerder had gehad.

Die typische visachtige lucht waar je van kokhalst als je je ondergoed naar beneden trekt.

Ik ging naar de huisarts. "Bacteriële vaginose. 

Heel normaal. Neem deze antibiotica."

Oké. No big deal.

Het werkte... voor ongeveer 10 dagen.

Toen hadden we weer seks.

En het was terug.

Deze cyclus herhaalde zich 8 maanden lang.

Ik ging telkens terug naar de huisarts. Kreeg telkens antibiotica. Zelfde verhaal.

Ons seksleven viel uit elkaar.

Niet omdat hij iets zei - hij was lief, begripvol.

Maar ik voelde me zo beschaamd dat ik seks begon te vermijden.

Ik verzon smoesjes:

"Ik ben moe."

"Ik voel me niet lekker."

"Laten we gewoon Netflix kijken."

Na een half jaar van dit gezeik zei hij: "Het voelt alsof je me niet meer wilt."

Ik wilde hem wel.

Maar ik wilde niet dat hij me... zo zou ruiken.

We gingen uit elkaar 3 maanden later.

Hij zei dat hij het gevoel had dat ik afstand hield.

En hij had gelijk.

Maar hoe leg je uit dat je je lichaam haat en tebeschaamd bent om intiem te zijn?

Na de break-up dacht ik: oké, nu ga ik dit echt oplossen.

Nieuwe start. Nieuw leven.

Ik ging naar een gynaecologe. Eindelijk een specialist.

Gynaecoloog 1: "Neem Metronidazol. Komt vaak voor."

Resultaat: Werkte 2 weken. Kwam terug.

Gynaecoloog 2: "Probeer Clindamycine. Soms werkt dat beter."

Resultaat: Werkte 10 dagen. Kwam terug.

I'm a 58-year-old retired physician's assistant. I worked in a family practice in Hartford for twenty-three years. I have referred women to HRT. Recommended supplements. Written prescriptions for cooling-related sleep aids. And once — for two years in 2018 and 2019 — actively dissuaded my own patients from looking into "Eastern medicine" because I did not consider it evidence-based.

That two-year stretch is the reason I am writing this.

The bracelet in the photo above has six therapeutic magnets on the inside surface, positioned exactly over the six acupressure meridians of the inner wrist. The mechanism is called **Meridian Magnetotherapy**. Eastern medicine has activated these six meridians with needles for two thousand years. The bracelet does it magnetically and continuously, without piercing the skin. It is sold by an American brand called Stamiri. It is hypoallergenic stainless steel. It is waterproof. You wear it twenty-four hours a day for as long as it takes your meridian wiring to come back online — typically four to eighteen months — and then you can take it off without symptoms returning.

I know how that sounds to someone who has spent a career in evidence-based American medicine. data.copy:
Een vrouw die ik al bijna een jaar alleen maar vriendelijk toeknikte in het verzorgingstehuis waar mijn moeder woont, kwam afgelopen oktober ineens aan mijn tafel zitten in de bezoekersruimte.

Ze zei:

*"Ik trek het niet om nóg een zondag alleen in deze ruimte door te brengen. Vind je het goed als ik bij je kom zitten?"*

Ik zei ja.

Twee uur later stond ze op om weg te gaan.

Maar voordat ze vertrok, had ze één zin uitgesproken die me sindsdien geen dag meer heeft losgelaten.

Ik schrijf deze brief omdat ik, in de achttien maanden vóór die zondag, in stilte voor twee mensen tegelijk zorgde.

Mijn zesentachtigjarige moeder, in haar kamer in een verzorgingstehuis op veertig minuten rijden van mijn huis.

En mijn zevenenzestigjarige man, thuis in onze woonkamer.

Die vrouw gaf me één van hen terug.

Mijn naam is **Johanna**.

Ik woon met mijn man **Gerard** in een klein dorpje vlak bij Zwolle.

We zijn inmiddels zevenendertig jaar getrouwd.

Gerard werkte eenenveertig jaar als projectmanager bij een fabriek.

Drie jaar geleden ging hij met pensioen.

We hebben een zoon en een dochter, allebei in de dertig en allebei op minder dan een uur rijden bij ons vandaan.

Zelf ging ik vier jaar geleden met pensioen, nadat ik tweeëndertig jaar de administratie had verzorgd voor onze kerk.

Op papier zouden dit de mooiste en rustigste jaren van ons leven moeten zijn.

Mijn moeder, **Riet**, is zesentachtig jaar.

Achttien maanden geleden viel ze in haar eigen keuken.

Ze brak haar heup.

Ze herstelde zoals iemand van zesentachtig nu eenmaal herstelt van zo'n breuk: grotendeels, maar nooit helemaal.

Sindsdien woont ze in een kleinschalig verzorgingstehuis dat **Lindehof** heet.

Mijn broer woont in Groningen en komt langs wanneer hij kan.

Ik ga iedere zondag bij haar op bezoek.

En soms ook op woensdag.

Ik neem altijd een zakje mandarijntjes voor haar mee, omdat ze daar al dol op is sinds ik een klein meisje was.

Sommige dingen herinnert ze zich nog feilloos.

excludeCountries.allowed_values: Comma-separated ISO2: US, GB, DK, NL, BE, IE, NO, SE, FR, DE, IT, CA, NZ, AU, BR, AT, CH, ES, FI, PL, PT, GR, TR, AE, SA, QA, KW, BH, OM, JO, IL, LB, IQ, EG.

storebasedin.description: Store Based In (dashboard storebasedin → store_traffic.shop_origin_country). Use for Mexico/Colombia/Chile/etc. store HQ.
storebasedin.allowed_values: Comma-separated ISO2 including MX, CO, CL, AR, PE and other Explore Shops Based In markets.

niches.description: Product category / vertical filter (dashboard Meta niches). Use when user asks for a category, niche, vertical, or market — not keyword.
niches.allowed_values: All, or comma-separated codes: CG, AM, GG, JY, GS, HT, BY, BG, SK, WC, MC, SP, KS, TS, HE, PS, DP, HI, FT, OG, OP, TR, AC, AA, BM, FK, SH, SW, EL, FW, WT, EW, FR, GM, PH, EC, WE, SC, BE, MU, PA, CB, CF, CP, DC, CT, HH, SG, YG, CC, PZ, LS, GP, WN, SF, OR, MG, PB. See allowed_niches in response for code→label map. Fashion/clothing = CG.

website.description: Detected store/checkout technology on the landing page (dashboard Website filter).
website.allowed_values: All, or comma-separated codes: SH, TP, BU, LS, CC, SL, TA, GG, FU, CS, LP, FO, SI, GP, XS, YC, HY, DI, MS, SB, PP, WC, TT, TW, PI, GO, SC, FB, MG, WP, SQ, PS, GM, KV, CO, HJ, WX, AR, BC, MC. SH=Shopify, WC=WooCommerce, CS=Clickfunnels. See allowed_technologies in response.

languages.allowed_values: All, or comma-separated: en, nl, de, no, fr, sv, da, it, pt, es, fi, pl, tr, ar, he.

excludeLanguages.allowed_values: Comma-separated: en, nl, de, no, fr, sv, da, it, pt, es, fi, pl, tr, ar, he.

apps.description: Shopify apps detected on the store.
apps.allowed_values: All, or comma-separated app names/ids from dashboard Apps filter. See allowed_apps in response.

excludeApps.description: Exclude stores using these Shopify apps.
excludeApps.allowed_values: Comma-separated app names/ids. See allowed_apps in response.

themes.description: Shopify theme name on the store (exact match).
themes.allowed_values: All, or comma-separated exact theme names from dashboard Themes filter (discover via GET /api/themes).

scaling.allowed_values: rising, stable, declining, nodownscaling, upscaling, downscaling.

mediafilter.allowed_values: videos, images, carousel, dco. Omit/All = all formats.

pagetypefilter.allowed_values: products, collections, funnels, nofunnels. Empty/All = all types.

adscorefilter.description: WinningHunter ad score tier (Established / Has Potential / Unestablished).
adscorefilter.allowed_values: winning (Established), scaling (Has Potential), testing (Unestablished). Requires matching account tier.

lowimpressions.description: Hide ads with very low impressions.
lowimpressions.allowed_values: hide (exclude low-impression rows). Omit = show all.

rankgrowthfilter.description: Within-brand ad rank momentum vs historic rank_history.
rankgrowthfilter.allowed_values: Comma-separated subset of: rising, stable, declining.

minadrank.description: Minimum within-brand ad rank (lower rank number = stronger ad for that brand, e.g. #1).

min.description: Minimum duplicate/active-seen ad count on the page.

minactiveads.description: Minimum active Meta ads on the advertiser Facebook page (total_active_ads_on_page).
minactiveads.notes: find_winning_products auto-applies minactiveads=50 for US when not set (see forced block).

minactiveadsgrowth.description: Minimum page active-ads percent growth over activeadsgrowthperiod.
minactiveadsgrowth.allowed_values: Human percent (25 = 25%); negatives allowed for decline.

activeadsgrowthperiod.description: Lookback window for active-ads growth filter.
activeadsgrowthperiod.allowed_values: 1w, 1m, 3m. Default 1m when min/max growth set. 1w=1 week, 1m=1 month, 3m=3 months.
activeadsgrowthperiod.notes: 14d/2m exist on the dashboard but are omitted from MCP — sparse wlads baselines return empty result sets.

minpagelikes.allowed_values: Integer >= 0. Ads missing the field excluded when min set.

minadspend.description: Minimum EU ad spend total in adspendtimeframe window.
minadspend.allowed_values: Integer >= 0. May require higher account tier; can return upgrade JSON.

maxadspend.description: Maximum EU ad spend in window.
maxadspend.allowed_values: Integer >= 0. 999999 treated as no upper cap server-side.

adspendtimeframe.description: Rolling window ad spend is summed over (NOT a calendar month filter).

minreach.description: Minimum EU reach/views total in reachtimeframe window.
minreach.allowed_values: Integer >= 0. May require higher account tier.

reachtimeframe.description: Rolling window reach is summed over.

mintraffic.allowed_values: Integer >= 0. May require higher account tier.

minproductsonstore.description: Minimum published products on the Shopify store.

minprice.description: Minimum product price on landing page.

mincopylength.description: Minimum ad primary text character length.

minvideolength.description: Minimum video duration in seconds (use with mediafilter=videos).

mindays.description: Minimum days the ad has been running.
mindays.allowed_values: Integer >= 0. May require higher account tier.

from.description: Ad launch date lower bound (Meta started field — when ad began running, NOT scrape date).
from.allowed_values: YYYY-MM-DD. Requires to on same range.

to.notes: To isolate ads running in a calendar month: ad_created_to=last day of month AND fromlastseen=first day of month.

product_from.description: Shopify product creation date lower bound.

pagefrom.description: Facebook page creation date lower bound.

activestatus.description: Legacy dashboard param (no longer applied to ES queries).
activestatus.allowed_values: Ignored — use adstatus or last_seen_from/to instead.

adstatus.description: Dashboard Status filter — recently seen vs stale ads.
adstatus.allowed_values: active (lastSeen or updated_at within last 4 days), inactive (neither field within last 4 days), All/empty (no status filter).
adstatus.notes: find_winning_products forces active. Same as dashboard Status = Active.

sorting.allowed_values: relevance, datefound, mostrecent, lastseen, adspend, longestrunning, reach, adsetamount, consistency, monthlyvisits, monthlytraffic, monthlyrevenue, pageactiveads, toprank, mostsaved. Aliases: rank/top_ad/best_ranked→toprank (asc = best rank first, desc = worst rank first). ad_started→mostrecent. monthly_visits→monthlyvisits. monthly_traffic→monthlytraffic.

page.description: Pagination page index (informational). Deep pagination requires scroll from the previous response — incrementing page alone does not advance the result set.
page.allowed_values: MCP uses 1-based page (1=first page); echoed value is 0-based internal page sent to API.

scroll.description: Opaque pagination cursor. Empty/omit on the first request; pass the response scroll value on the next request with the same filters to fetch more ads. Required to download beyond the first page (especially sort_by=lastseen).
scroll.allowed_values: Opaque string from previous response; empty string or omit for first page. Stop when scroll is null/absent or data is shorter than a full page.
